title: From Random Quantum Codes to Explicit qLDPC Codes via Local Properties
authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo, Xiaojuan Ma, Nikhil Shagrithaya
abstract: Constructing explicit codes matching the parameters of random codes has been a central and largely elusive question in coding theory. The quantum setting is even more challenging since it is highly desirable that the quantum code be an LDPC code.   Local coordinate-wise linear (LCL) [Levi, Mosheiff, and Shagrithaya, FOCS 2025] witnesses provide a unifying language for many coding-theoretic properties, from distance to list decoding and list recovery. In particular, it provides a framework to study properties of random linear codes, which achieve optimal parameters for many properties of linear codes.   For CSS quantum codes, however, a local witness has two distinct ranks: its physical rank before quotienting by stabilizers and its logical rank after quotienting. We develop a quantum version of the LCL framework for nested spaces $S \subseteq C$, in which local constraints are imposed on physical representatives while independence is measured in the logical quotient $C/S$. The resulting theory gives a threshold theorem for random CSS codes, and as a consequence shows that the per-sector rate threshold is equal to the classical rate threshold. We also define a quantum analogue of subspace design [Guruswami and Xing, STOC 2013] and show that they can be described in a natural manner within the quantum-LCL framework.   Finally, we give explicit constructions for arbitrary folded quantum-LCL properties, in a manner similar to the LCL derandomization of [Jeronimo and Shagrithaya, STOC 2026]. As a consequence, we obtain the first explicit constructions of quantum list-decodable codes and list-recoverable codes that have optimal list sizes, in addition to explicit quantum subspace design codes. We note that all our explicit constructions are qLDPC codes, an important property for quantum error-correcting codes.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of finding explicit quantum error-correcting codes that achieve the optimal performance bounds known for random quantum codes. By developing a quantum version of the LCL framework, the authors establish theoretical thresholds and provide concrete, explicit constructions for quantum list-decodable and list-recoverable codes. These resulting codes are all of the desirable qLDPC type.
main_problem: The central goal is to construct explicit quantum error-correcting codes, specifically qLDPC codes, whose optimal properties match those of theoretically ideal random quantum codes.
main_result: The authors provide explicit constructions for quantum list-decodable and list-recoverable codes with optimal list sizes, all of which are proven to be qLDPC codes.
method: They develop a quantum analogue of the Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) framework for nested quantum spaces, adapting the Alon–Edmonds–Luby (AEL) local-to-global paradigm to derandomize theoretical guarantees into concrete constructions.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum error correction codes, particularly CSS quantum codes, analyzed using the qLCL framework for nested subspaces $S \subseteq C$. The underlying structure involves stabilizer codes and their logical quotients.
key_observables: Code parameters (rate, distance, list sizes), quantum ranks (physical vs. logical), and threshold values for decoding.
important_parameters: The construction depends on achieving optimal list sizes and maintaining the qLDPC structure, relating to the rate $R$ and error parameters $ho$.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on adapting classical coding-theoretic tools (like LCL witnesses) to the quantum setting, and the final constructions assume the existence of explicit outer CSS families with desired properties.
paper_structure: The paper builds theory by introducing the quantum-LCL framework, deriving threshold theorems for random CSS codes, defining quantum subspace designs, and culminating in explicit constructions for various quantum list-decodable/recoverable properties.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical bridge between the theoretical existence of optimal quantum codes (random codes) and the practical requirement of having explicit, structured codes (qLDPC codes), which is crucial for building physical quantum hardware.
